1.0.0.en: It is evident from the words of St. Luke that many in his time had written about the life of Christ in addition to the Evangelists. Since Luke believed in Christ after having been a Gentile, and attached himself to the Apostles who had witnessed the life of the Lord Jesus and had become ministers of the Word, he felt a responsibility to write about His life as well, because he had followed it with precision. His work as a physician, accustomed to examination and exactness, helped him in this.

1.0.1.en: This means that Luke gathered his information from two sources:

1.0.2.en: (1) The Virgin and the disciples who witnessed Christ.

1.0.3.en: (2) The writings of the many who preceded him, though their writings may have been incomplete.

1.0.4.en: Here the importance of Church Tradition becomes clear, that is, the oral Apostolic handing down of the faith from the Fathers the Apostles to their disciples until it reached us today. This includes the text of the Holy Bible and all the faith and rites of the Church. It is Tradition that has preserved the Church from the days of the Apostles until now.

1.0.5.en: May you become accustomed to exactness in understanding the Holy Bible and all the faith and rites of the Church, and may you also examine your own life with exactness in repentance, so that you may grow strongly in the spiritual life.

1.1.0.en: Since Luke took care to know the details of the life of Christ, he wrote the life of Christ in order to Theophilus, who had believed and been taught much, so as to confirm his faith in Christ. He was a Greek who had become a Christian and was living in Alexandria, and he held a great political position, for Luke calls him "most excellent," that is, His Excellency; and the meaning of his name is "lover of God." So if you, my brother, are a lover of God, this Gospel is addressed to you, as St. Ambrose says.

1.2.0.en: This chapter has a special importance, because it is the preparation for the birth of Christ; therefore the Church reads it on the four Sundays of the month of Koiak before the Feast of the Nativity. It tells us:

1.2.1.en: The first Sunday: the annunciation of the birth of John.

1.2.2.en: The second Sunday: the annunciation of the birth of Christ.

1.2.3.en: The third Sunday: the Virgin's visit to Elisabeth.

1.2.4.en: The fourth Sunday: the birth of John the Baptist.

1.2.5.en: Herod: the king mentioned is Herod the Great, who was a descendant of Esau and hated the Jews. He ruled from 37 BC until about 4 BC. His reign was marked by cruelty, and before the end of his life he killed the children of Bethlehem (the birth of Christ was in 4 BC, and the children were killed when He was a few months old). He ruled all the land of the Jews.

1.2.6.en: Zacharias: it means "God remembers," and he was a priest.

1.2.7.en: Elisabeth: that is, "the oath of God," and she was also of the descendants of Aaron the high priest.

1.2.8.en: They were distinguished by righteousness in fulfilling God's commandments and likewise His ordinances, which are the requirements of the Law. All this is sound spiritual conduct, visible before men. In addition to that, their hearts were pure before God. Because of their righteousness, God chose to speak to them after His speech with His people had ceased for more than three centuries, so that they might bear John, whose name means "God is gracious."

1.2.9.en: "Thus the love of God appears toward everyone who fears Him. If you hold fast to God's commandments and to your spiritual striving, you will see His tenderness and His many graces.

1.2.10.en: The course of Abia: in the time of Zacharias there were about 20,000 priests in Judea, divided into 24 courses, each of about a thousand, and each course served in the Temple for a week twice a year.

1.3.0.en: Despite the righteousness of Zacharias and Elisabeth, they faced a difficult problem, namely childlessness, because barrenness was considered a disgrace in the Old Testament, as a sign of unworthiness to bear the awaited Messiah. They had grown old, and there was no longer any hope of having children. But God's wisdom in the affliction appeared afterward, for the delay in childbearing was so that God might give them John the Baptist ... the greatest of those born of women, who prepares the way of Christ, and who had to be born six months before Christ.

1.4.s.en: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

1.4.0.en: The week of service of the course of Abia came, and the priests attended, among them the aged Zacharias, and the lot was cast as usual to determine who would enter to offer incense on the golden altar inside the sanctuary, which no one but the priests were permitted to enter.

1.4.1.en: The lot usually came to a priest no more than once in a lifetime, to enter this great place and offer incense to God, because the number of the course, as we mentioned, was a thousand.

1.4.2.en: The multitude of the people stood outside the sanctuary, waiting for the blessing of Zacharias the priest after he had burned incense inside the sanctuary.

1.4.3.en: How great is God's grace in the New Testament, which allows all the priests to enter the sanctuary every day and offer incense in the sight of all the people, and even to come out with the incense to bless all who are present in the Church, because the burning of the incense and its sweet fragrance are a type of the death of Christ on the Cross to take away our sins. For this reason our prayers rise in thanksgiving and praise with this incense ascending to heaven.

1.5.0.en: The lot fell on Zacharias, and this was by divine providence ... for when he entered the sanctuary and offered incense on the golden altar in the middle of the sanctuary, before the veil of the Holy of Holies, in which was the ark of the covenant, and then bowed down as the priests were accustomed to do, and rose, a luminous angel of majestic form appeared to him on the right side of the altar of incense. The altar of incense: there were two main altars in Solomon's temple. The first was outside, and sacrifices and offerings were presented on it; the second was inside, and nothing was offered on it but incense, which was also considered an offering and was called "a sweet savour unto the Lord."

1.5.1.en: From the altar and the Temple divine graces and heavenly blessings are poured out upon us, so that we receive the greatest thing, the Body and Blood of the Lord, and acquire peace and joy ... and our inward eyes are opened to see God and to enjoy fellowship with Him together with all the heavenly ones.

1.6.0.en: Before the grandeur of this heavenly appearance, Zacharias was afraid, so the angel reassured him and declared to him that God had cared for his prayers for tens of years until now, not only for the begetting of offspring but also for his longing for the coming of Christ. For as a priest he prayed thus in his liturgical prayers, awaiting the divine Incarnation. The angel promised him that his aged wife would conceive, and even announced the name of the child, "John," that is, God's grace.

1.6.1.en: How reassuring to the soul is God's care for every prayer and petition we raise to Him, yet He answers at the proper time. So continue, my brother, in your prayers however much the answer is delayed, confident that it will be answered in the fitting way, at the best time that God sees for you.

1.7.0.en: The angel declared that John was not an ordinary child who would gladden only the hearts of his aged parents, relatives and neighbors, but that his ministry would extend to become joy for everyone who believes and responds to his call.

1.8.0.en: For he shall be great: John will become great in the sight of the Lord, and will be appointed a Nazarite to God.

1.8.1.en: And shall drink neither wine nor strong drink: he will not drink fermented grape juice nor intoxicating wine.

1.8.2.en: He shall be filled with the Holy Ghost: he is distinguished from the rest of mankind by being filled with the Holy Spirit while still an unborn child; therefore he is the greatest of those born of women, as Christ Himself declared (Mt 11:11).

1.9.0.en: The angel speaks about the nature of John's ministry, which is calling the Jews to repentance and return to God, and the return of love and unity within the family between fathers and children, and calling sinners and the disobedient to God's commandments so that they may repent and think of righteousness.

1.9.1.en: And this is the preparation for the divine Incarnation. For when the angel declares that John goes before his God, this is a proof of the divinity of Christ, whose ministry begins six months after him; and he also declares that John will be strong in the manner of his ministry like Elijah the prophet.

1.10.0.en: Zacharias' mind could not believe the divine good news, and he presented his reasons, namely that he and his wife were aged and it was impossible for them to bear a child. Yet history had repeatedly shown the ability of the aged to bear children by God's miraculous work, such as Abraham and Sarah, and barrenness had not stood in the way, as with Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob and Rachel, and Manoah and his wife, the parents of Samson. But the gentleness of Zacharias is to be noted: he did not complain about his wife's barrenness, but said courteously that she was well stricken in years.

1.11.0.en: The day that these things shall be performed: that is, the birth of John the Baptist, for eight days after it Zacharias spoke. So "the day" means the time or period of his birth, and not specifically the day of birth.

1.11.1.en: Because of Zacharias' doubt he lost his ability to speak, as the archangel Gabriel, meaning "the might of God," declared to him; he is one of the seven archangels who stand before God. His silence was the natural result of not believing the voice of God. The silence of Zacharias declares the silence of the Old Testament, so that the New Testament might begin with Jesus Christ; Jewish worship fell silent and became meaningless after the coming of Christ and the cessation of the prophets among them.

1.12.0.en: The people were waiting for Zacharias to bless them according to the custom of Jewish worship, but the vision took a long time, so the multitude marveled, asking the reason for his delay.

1.13.0.en: When Zacharias came out unable to speak, content only with signs of his hands, they understood that he had seen a vision inside the sanctuary as used to happen with the prophets of old. So they rejoiced at the divine revelation, although they longed to know this revelation, which remained obscure because of Zacharias' silence.

1.14.0.en: Zacharias remained in the Temple until the week of his service ended, then returned to his house, which was outside Jerusalem in the hills surrounding the city.

1.15.0.en: When Elisabeth felt that she had conceived, she and her husband Zacharias rejoiced greatly and thanked God who had blessed them, and Elisabeth was finally relieved of the women's reproaches against her for barrenness and unworthiness of blessing. But she hid herself for five months from appearing before people so as to be certain of the miraculous conception, for she had shared her husband in the sin of doubt.

1.15.1.en: But this period in which Zacharias was silent was an opportunity for a deeper conversation with God, in which repentance was mingled with thanksgiving, and also meditation on God's earlier works with His people and with them.

1.15.2.en: Take advantage of the opportunity of illness and of your being sometimes apart from people to review yourself and offer repentance, thanksgiving and meditation on God's works with you. You can feel this if you take a weekly retreat.

1.16.s.en: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

1.16.0.en: Six months after the archangel Gabriel's announcement to Zacharias, at the beginning of the sixth month, he appeared in a small town called Nazareth, which is in Galilee, that is, the northern part of the land of the Jews, and is more than 80 miles from Jerusalem. It lay on a trade route and was visited by Gentile merchants and Roman soldiers, so it was known for its distance from Jewish worship because of the many Gentiles in it. There, in a small house, was a virgin about fifteen years of age named Mary, living in the care of an old man named Joseph of the tribe of David [so that the prophecies would be fulfilled that Christ would be the son of David (Ps 132:11)], and he worked as a carpenter, but his livelihood was poor because of his old age and weakness for work. Betrothal in Jewish society was considered a formal marriage bond, but without the beginning of the physical relationship, as is the case now among our Muslim brethren in what is called "writing the contract," which is a formal marriage without the physical relationship.

1.17.0.en: The angel gave peace to the Virgin, and it is God's gift in which His children alone are distinguished from the rest of the world: "There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked" (Isa 57:21). He described her as full of grace (as in the Coptic and Greek text, which was mistranslated in the Beirut edition as "highly favored"), unlike the rest of mankind, who are favored with His blessings, whereas the Holy Spirit came upon her and filled her with grace so that the Holy God might be born of her, and He made her blessed and blessed her among all women. And as sin entered the world through Eve, so the good news of salvation came through a woman, the Virgin Mary.

1.18.0.en: The sight of the angel was majestic, so the young Virgin was afraid of his splendor and light, and thought in herself about the reason for his appearing, his greeting and his blessing her.

1.19.0.en: The angel reassured her of God's love for her and His intention to bestow on her the greatest blessings because of her holiness and her attachment to God. The angel also announced to her the good news of the divine conception, and the name of the God who became man, which is Jesus, and the meaning of His name is Savior.

1.20.0.en: He described Him with an attribute of God, which is "greatness," and even named Him "the Son of the Highest," that is, the Son of God, of His essence and nature, and in Him all the prophecies are fulfilled, for He is the awaited Messiah of the seed of David.

1.21.0.en: So that Christ may be King forever over Jacob, that is, God's people who believe in Him.

1.21.1.en: Christ wants to reign over your heart and let you enjoy His love forever, if you believe in Him, submit to Him and obey His commandments.

1.22.s.en: (7) The Virgin's dialogue with the angel

1.22.0.en: The Virgin Mary accepted the divine good news and believed, as Elisabeth later testified (Lk 1:

1.22.1.en: 45), but she had vowed virginity, so her question was whether God wanted her to give up her virginity, for she said to the angel, "I know not a man."

1.23.0.en: The angel's answer confirmed that she would keep her virginity, so that she would be ever-virgin, because God had prepared a miraculous way to accomplish this divine conception, which is the coming of the Holy Spirit upon her to form the first complete cell of the embryo within the womb, and the power of the Highest overshadowing is the embrace of the Father for accomplishing the divine begetting. Then he clearly declares the eternal attribute of the One to be born, for He is the Holy One, that is, God and the Son of God, being of His nature and essence.

1.24.0.en: When God saw her wonderful faith and her submission to the good news, despite the many sufferings she would endure, because she would be accused of fornication by all those around her, He supported her with the good news of the conception of Elisabeth her aged kinswoman, to confirm her faith in God's miraculous power; for He is able to make the aged barren woman pregnant, and He is also able to do all things, so that He makes the virgin conceive.

1.25.0.en: The Virgin's answer at the close of this dialogue was submission to the good news in complete surrender and wonderful humility. She did not boast that she was the Mother of God, but declared that she was His handmaid.

1.25.1.en: To the extent that you obey God's commandments and rely on Him in surrendering your life to Him, the blessings of heaven overflow upon you, and God supports you and confirms your faith, and you behold God in your life, so that you are reassured and rejoice and become worthy to behold the heavenly things while you are on earth.

1.26.0.en: In those days, that is, a little after the angel's announcement to her; that is, she prepared herself for the journey immediately after the annunciation.

1.26.1.en: Into the hill country: the Virgin traveled a long distance from Nazareth in Galilee, north of Judea, to the region of Jerusalem, to a city near it belonging to the tribe of Judah, and bore the hardships of the journey, crossing the mountains to reach Elisabeth.

1.26.2.en: Since the Virgin Mary was filled with the divine good news, and the divine Child had come to dwell in her womb, she who was full of grace hastened with spiritual zeal, climbing the mountains, in search of someone to whom she might give her love, which she would offer to all humanity through her only-begotten Son. She went to Elisabeth not only to congratulate her but to serve her, because she was pregnant and aged and needed someone to help her. She is the Church that preaches Christ the Savior of the world.

1.27.0.en: When the Virgin entered the house of her kinswoman Elisabeth, the wife of Zacharias the priest, she gave her the peace which is God's gift to His children.

1.28.0.en: When Elisabeth heard the greeting, the child in her womb bowed down before Jesus who was in the womb of the Virgin, and leaped with joy at this meeting, and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, who revealed to her many things: (1) That the Virgin was pregnant with the awaited Messiah, that is, Jesus Christ.

1.28.1.en: (2) That the movement of the child in her womb was worship and joy at the meeting of Christ and the Virgin His mother.

1.29.0.en: Elisabeth said to the Virgin that she was worthy of blessing more than all the women of the world, and that the child in her womb was also blessed. With evident humility Elisabeth declared her unworthiness that the Mother of God should visit her. This was a support and confirmation of the Virgin's faith in the divine good news, which she had told to no one, and it was also a declaration by the Church, represented in Elisabeth, of the Virgin's position as the Mother of God.

1.30.0.en: Elisabeth offered the proof of the Virgin's greatness, which was the movement and worship of the child John in her womb when the Virgin greeted her.

1.31.0.en: In humility also, Elisabeth confessed her sin and her husband's in not believing the angel's good news, whereas the Virgin was distinguished from them by her wonderful faith in a good news the like of which had never been heard before, a virgin conceiving. Elisabeth knew of the angel's announcement to the Virgin through the Holy Spirit who came upon her. May you be humble, confessing your sins before others and esteeming them above yourself in honor, so that you may deserve God's blessings and blessed fruits may come forth from you like John, that is, holy virtues.

1.32.0.en: If sin entered the world through Eve, now women, Elisabeth and the Virgin, come forward with joyful prophecies about the blessed Christ, the Savior of the world.

1.32.1.en: As the Virgin meditates on God, His image grows great and magnified within her, and she rejoices in Him as her personal Savior from her sins; for she needed salvation like the rest of mankind, even though she is the greatest of the saints and even above the angels because of her holiness and virtues.

1.33.0.en: The Virgin showed God's wonderful grace which He gave her, declaring her humility as God's handmaid, whom He condescended to regard and granted to be His mother; therefore all mankind praises her.

1.34.0.en: God who is almighty gave me, while I was a virgin, to conceive; and it is likewise among the greatness of His works that He united with humanity in the mystery of the Incarnation when He is as a child in my womb, and He is also able to bind Satan on the Cross for the redemption of mankind; and despite His humbling Himself by His Incarnation, He is the Holy God.

1.35.0.en: In the preceding verse the Virgin described God as mighty and holy, and here she speaks of His mercy which He grants to everyone who believes in Him and fears Him, not only in this generation but to the end of days, for His salvation He offers to all mankind.

1.36.0.en: God's power appears in making the humble Virgin conceive, and likewise the aged Elisabeth, whereas the proud, such as Herod, He scatters all their power and evil, and they cannot harm the Christ who is born, just as He scatters the demons and binds them with His Cross.

1.37.0.en: Everyone who is proud and esteems himself, He brings down from the material position in which he has placed himself, like Herod who was eaten by worms (the son of Herod the Great); and at the same time He glorifies the humble, like the Virgin and Elisabeth.

1.38.0.en: Everyone who hungers for righteousness, He satisfies with His most holy Body and Blood and every spiritual gift, but those who rely on their riches and the money of the world receive no blessing from Him and have no share in the Kingdom of Heaven.

1.39.0.en: The Virgin adds to her glorification of God a fourth attribute in Him, which is His faithfulness to His promises to His people Israel, whom she calls "servant," that is, a son whom God his Father cares for and supports, so He offers him salvation through His Incarnation and redemption, and then the children of God remember His mercy and thank Him at all times.

1.39.1.en: And the people of God are not only the old Israel but the new Israel, that is, the Christians who believe in Him, whether Jews or Gentiles. The fulfillment of the promises He gave to Abraham and the fathers, that is, salvation, lasts forever with His children who believe in Him, so that they rejoice with Him in His heavenly Kingdom.

1.39.2.en: The shortest road to God's heart is humility, by knowing your sins and your need of Him; then all the heavenly blessings pour down upon you. So hold yourself to account, offer repentance before Him every day, and humble yourself also before everyone, and He will raise you above all with inner peace and happiness on earth, and then with heavenly glories in the age to come.

1.40.0.en: The Virgin Mary remained for three months humbly serving the aged Elisabeth, who was in the last months of her pregnancy, forgetting her great position. And since the child John had leaped for joy in Elisabeth's womb merely at meeting the Christ-child in the Virgin's womb, how great was the joy and fulfillment of Elisabeth and John when they enjoyed the company of the Virgin and her Son for three whole months!

1.40.1.en: After that the Virgin returned to her home in the town of Nazareth in Galilee, where her pregnancy became evident and Joseph discovered it, as Matthew the Evangelist mentions (Mt 1).

1.41.s.en: (10) The birth and ministry of John

1.41.0.en: At last Elisabeth's nine months were completed and she bore her son, and when her loved ones heard of it they rejoiced greatly, because the Lord's miracle had been accomplished in the conception of the aged barren woman.

1.42.0.en: On the eighth day, when a male child of the people of Israel is circumcised, which is a proof of sonship to God and was a type of Baptism. It was the custom to name the child on the day of his circumcision, so the relatives who had gathered called him Zacharias after the name of his father.

1.43.0.en: But his mother, who was filled with the Holy Spirit, said that he should be called John. She had learned that name from his father Zacharias, according to what the angel had declared to him; so he must have written this name for her, and even the details of the vision, so that she might rejoice with him in it.

1.44.0.en: The relatives who had gathered objected, since this name was foreign to the names of the family; for it was customary to use certain names in each family so that they might be blessed and imitate their forefathers, and so that no one afterward would doubt the new son's belonging to his family.

1.45.0.en: Those present made signs to his father, who was mute and had probably also lost his hearing; therefore they did not speak to him but made signs to him, asking him what he wanted his son to be called.

1.46.0.en: Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote on it John, and those present were greatly astonished at the agreement of the parents on one name. Perhaps it was also a revelation from the angel to Zacharias of the child's name. They usually used tablets of wood covered with wax on which they wrote with a stylus pointed at one end to engrave in the wax and flat at its other end to erase what they wished to erase.

1.47.0.en: Immediately after he wrote the name John, God healed him and his tongue was loosed, praising God, and the fear of God fell on the hearts of those present when Zacharias spoke. His opinion agreed with his wife Elisabeth about this strange name, John, and the news of this miracle spread throughout Jerusalem and the hill country of Judea surrounding it.

1.48.0.en: Everyone felt that this child was no ordinary one and would be great; and as they recalled the events of his wonderful birth, they began to think about the manifestations of spiritual greatness that would appear in him when he grew up. Observe God's works with those around you, and try to learn something from them for yourself that will bring you closer to God, for they are messages from Him to you every day.

1.49.s.en: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

1.49.0.en: During the nine months of silence, Zacharias enjoyed many prayers and meditations with God, so he became worthy to be filled with the Holy Spirit, and speaks to us about Christ and the salvation that He would accomplish on the Cross and declare by the power of His Resurrection.

1.50.0.en: Zacharias blessed God and called Him the God of Israel to declare His fatherhood and care for His people, for He had finally fulfilled His promises to Abraham and the fathers by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption on the Cross.

1.51.0.en: Christ the Savior is the Son of David, who established a strong spiritual kingdom symbolized by the horn (which is the strongest thing in an animal), which defeats our enemies, that is, the demons who hate us.

1.52.0.en: By the mouth of his holy prophets: God is the One who speaks through the mouth of the prophets, so submission to the word of God is necessary. Since the world began: from the beginning of creation, that is, from Adam until this time.

1.52.1.en: By this the prophecies of all the prophets about Christ, and all of God's oaths and promises, were fulfilled.

1.53.0.en: From this verse to v. 75 he begins to describe the effectiveness of Christ's salvation and its effect on those who believe in Him. He declares that He frees us from the dominion of sin, to which the demons draw us, for it hates us and tries to ensnare us, but by His power we repel its attacks.

1.54.0.en: The salvation of Christ is not only for the living who believe in Him, but also mercy and redemption for all the fathers who died in hope, believing in the awaited Messiah.

1.54.1.en: For God remembers His promises to the fathers, that is, He carries them out and transfers them from Hades to Paradise, by His salvation which He accomplishes on the Cross.

1.55.0.en: The covenant or divine oath which He promised to Abraham the father of the fathers (Gen 22:16, 17), He now fulfills in Christ our Savior.

1.56.0.en: Christ gives those who believe in Him peace and assurance, so that they are not troubled by the wars of the demons, nor do they fear them, because He rescues them from them; and as they enjoy this peace, they go forth in spiritual worship of God.

1.57.0.en: The worship we offer to God is to be in holiness, that is, inward purity and righteousness that appears in the purity of our conduct, because we offer it to God who searches the hearts and reins and who sees all our works throughout our lives. Remember, my brother, that if you have received freedom and the new nature in Baptism, your only goal in your life is to worship God and walk in righteousness, and any evil you do is a departure from your life, which is devoted and consecrated to the love of God and doing good.

1.58.0.en: Zacharias continues his prophecy and addresses the child John, calling him the prophet of God, whereas Christ called John more than a prophet (ch. 7:26); and the function of John the Baptist is to prepare the way of Christ in the hearts of his people.

1.59.0.en: The Jews thought that Christ would save them from the slavery of the Romans, so John came to make known to them the true salvation, which is salvation from sin by repentance so that they might receive the forgiveness of their sins. So John makes known to them salvation and calls them to repentance, while Christ is the One who accomplishes this salvation on the Cross.

1.60.0.en: Zacharias returns to speak about Christ the Savior, and declares God's deep love, which is expressed by the mercy springing from His bowels. This mercy visited mankind in the fullness of time to rescue it from the darkness of sin, by the Incarnation of Christ, who is the Sun of Righteousness coming from heaven.

1.61.0.en: Christ is the light of the world; He shines on sinners who are preoccupied with the lusts of the world, expressed by darkness, and as He lights for them the way of life with Him, He guides them to the way of the Kingdom, so that they enjoy inner peace when He frees them from sin, and they even remain in this peace forever.

1.61.1.en: God visits you today with His tender love, you who sit in the darkness of sin. May you repent of your beloved sin, and may your heart be lifted up with feelings of love in repentance and thanksgiving, prepared to receive His love poured out on the altar in His most holy Body and Blood.

1.62.0.en: After the prophecy of Zacharias, St. Luke concludes his account with the growth of John, bodily and spiritually, with God's help in the wilderness. Tradition tells us how, at the killing of the firstborn of Bethlehem, Zacharias carried him to the altar in the Temple of God, and an angel came and snatched him away to live in the wilderness in the care of the angels.

1.62.1.en: As for Zacharias, whom the Roman soldiers were pursuing, they seized him and killed him between the Temple and the altar (Mt 23:35). In the stillness of the wilderness, John's love, prayers and meditations grew, and God prepared him to be His forerunner. He remained there until the age of thirty, which is the legal age for beginning ministry among the Jews, when he began his preaching. The birth of Jesus, His circumcision and His entry into the Temple
